references.text: Protoevangelium: God's promise that the woman's offspring will crush the serpent's head – the background for the authority to tread on snakes.
God led Israel through the wilderness with poisonous snakes and scorpions – the same word pair (snakes and scorpions) is used here.
"Over løve og slange skal du skride, du skal tråkke på ungløve og orm" – a direct parallel to treading on snakes and dangerous creatures.
The serpent as the enemy – here the serpent is introduced as God's adversary, which underlies why "the enemy" in Luke 10:19 is identified with the serpent/Satan.
In the messianic kingdom, a nursing child will play at the cobra's den – an image of complete protection against the power of snakes.
Jesus promised that believers would pick up snakes and not be harmed – a parallel to the promise of authority over snakes and that nothing shall harm them.
Jesus gave the twelve authority (ἐξουσία) over unclean spirits – the same type of transfer of power to the disciples.
Jesus gave the twelve power and authority over all evil spirits – a direct precursor in the Gospel of Luke to the authority given to the seventy in 10:19.
Paul was bitten by a poisonous snake on Malta but suffered no harm – a concrete fulfillment of the promise that "nothing shall harm you".
"The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet" – a parallel to trampling the enemy underfoot with God's authority.
Christ is set above all power and authority – the supreme authority that also provides the basis for the authority received by the disciples.
The believers' struggle is against the spiritual hosts of wickedness – "the enemy's power" in Luke 10:19 points to these same spiritual adversaries.
The ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan – identifies the serpent with the enemy over whom the disciples have authority.
Scorpions are mentioned as an image of demonic torment – a parallel to the scorpions mentioned in Luke 10:19.
"The evil one shall not touch him" – a parallel to the promise that nothing shall harm believers.
